title: Why Is Microwave Food Still Cold in the Middle?
caption: Microwaves don't cook from the inside out. They heat the outer few centimeters, and the middle only catches up later.
pinned_comment: Do you stir halfway, or are you team lava-and-ice? 👇

lines.text: Lava on the edges, ice in the middle?
That's because a microwave doesn't cook from the inside out.
Inside, a part called a magnetron turns electricity into radio waves.
The waves bounce around the metal box and flip direction about two and a half billion times a second.
Water molecules are lopsided, slightly negative on one end, slightly positive on the other.
So every flip makes them twist back and forth, like tiny compass needles.
All that twisting rubs against their neighbors and turns into heat.
But the waves only reach a couple of centimeters into the food.
The center only warms up later, as heat slowly spreads inward.
That's why big portions stay icy in the middle, and why the plate keeps turning.
And the mesh in the door? Its holes are smaller than the waves, so they stay in, but light gets out.

visual.label: wavelength, far bigger than the holes
